summary:
Meet Ganston, a space explorer tasked with ensuring his team makes it through different space missions! 

We didn't just build a game, but created a simulation that highlights the different challenges of space missions and their difficulties. 

Ganston is presented with questions formed with NASA data, based on real space missions and events that occured during them. 

Every decision has consequences, just like in real space mission design. You must manage 4 different resources for Ganston's missions; fuel, energy, material and the teams happiness, and ensure they all stay above zero while also progressing and earning mission percent. 

The goal of our game is to create an interactive and fun experience for all ages that allows users to enjoy themselves, while also learning about the difficulties and challenges presented in real space mission design. 

We wanted to present players with both success and failures from past missions as our chosen Space Data, in hopes that we can all learn from the mistakes and successes of the past, and improve as we move into the age of this new frontier. 

Thank you and we hope you enjoy your adventure along with Ganston!
details:
What is Ganston the Space Explorer

Ganston the Space Explorer is a Space Mission design simulator created in Scratch 3.0! We were inspired by a mini-game from the website Blooket called Crazy Kingdom! This game involves being asked yes or no questions, which gives you different consequences/rewards based on your response. This game seemed appropriate for basing our game after, as after our research we became absolutely certain of one thing: all decisions have consequences!

This statement sort of became the slogan behind our game, as we found that a lot of failed missions we learned of during our research and data collection came from tiny mistakes or miscommunications between teams or mismanaged resources.

We aimed to create a game that both simulated the challenges and difficulties that come with designing a real space mission, but also highlights the amazing amazing missions of the past, present and now the future as we venture into this new frontier in the technological age!

Problems and Potential Improvements

We definitely had some problems when brainstorming and trying to design this game. We first had some disagreements about what to program the game in, as some of our team members wanted to do Scratch but others had lots of experience in Python.

We also all agree we could improve in our implementation of data. We think we did a pretty good job of displaying the challenges of managing resources in a space mission, but didn't feel we did amazing with using data.

We mainly used data with forming the questions, as well as in the "character select" where you choose a certain mission to start with which alters your stats. We created some infographics that shows players how our research of different space missions inspired our questions, but in retrospect we wish we found a way to incorporate larger data sets and databases to provide possibly more realistic questions for space simulations.

That being said, we are extremely super super super proud of Ganston the Space Explorer and truly believe our game can help make a difference and inspire people of all ages and walks of life!

Software/Programs

Scratch 3.0 - Programming Language

Piskel - Sprite Creation and Background design

Claude - Help sort data to form some of our questions and data for our infographs

Canva - Title Screen, Win Screen, Lose Screen
